stem: A 9-year-old boy has a tender swelling in the right axilla for 5 days with low-grade fever and headache. He was scratched by a new kitten 2 weeks ago. Biopsy of the node shows granulomas with central stellate microabscesses, and a silver stain shows small pleomorphic rods.
oneliner: 9M + tender axillary node + fever + kitten scratch 2 weeks ago + stellate microabscesses + silver stain rods → ?
ask: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

whyNot.B: Sarcoidosis has **noncaseating granulomas with no organism**; here a silver stain shows rods and microabscesses
whyNot.C: TB has **caseation and acid-fast bacilli**; this node has stellate microabscesses with silver-stained rods
whyNot.D: A foreign body granuloma contains **polarizable material**, not microabscesses and rods
whyNot.E: CGD shows **recurrent deep infections in childhood** with catalase-positive organisms, not a single node after a scratch

why: A **kitten scratch** followed by regional lymphadenopathy, with **stellate microabscesses and silver-stained rods**, is Bartonella henselae infection. It is self-limited in most immunocompetent children.

stem: A 4-year-old girl has 2 weeks of diarrhea and fever. CT shows enlarged mesenteric and para-aortic lymph nodes. A node biopsy shows caseating granulomas containing acid-fast bacilli. Serum IgG, IgA and IgM and B and T cell counts are normal.
oneliner: 4F + diarrhea + mesenteric nodes + caseating granulomas with acid-fast bacilli + normal T and B cells → ?
ask: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

whyNot.A: Sarcoidosis has **noncaseating granulomas without organisms**; hers caseate and contain acid-fast bacilli
whyNot.B: IFN-gamma receptor deficiency leaves macrophages unactivated, so **no granulomas form**; her node has caseating granulomas
whyNot.C: CGD gives **catalase-positive** infections such as S. aureus and Aspergillus; her granulomas contain acid-fast bacilli
whyNot.D: Cat-scratch shows **stellate microabscesses with silver-stained rods**; hers are caseating granulomas with acid-fast bacilli

why: **Caseating granulomas with acid-fast bacilli** mean mycobacteria held in check by an intact Th1 response: macrophage IL-12 drives Th1 cells to make IFN-gamma, which activates macrophages to wall off the organism. Normal T and B cells fit a child who can build granulomas.

set_title: Sharp chest pain after a virus: pericardium, myocardium, pleura or chest wall
stem: A 14-year-old boy has had fever for 2 days and now has sudden, sharp right-sided chest pain that is worse with breathing. A coxsackie B outbreak is occurring at his school. Pleurodynia and acute pericarditis are both being considered.
oneliner: 14M + 2 days of fever + sudden sharp chest pain worse with breathing + coxsackie B outbreak at school → pleurodynia or pericarditis?
ask: Which single finding favours pleurodynia over acute pericarditis?

options.D: Exposure to a coxsackie B outbreak

why: Coxsackie B can inflame the pericardium or the chest-wall muscles. In pleurodynia (Bornholm disease) the pain comes from muscle, so **the intercostal muscles are tender to pressure**, the ECG is normal and no rub is heard; pericarditis gives a rub, PR depression and diffuse ST elevation.

set_title: Shock: which type from the hemodynamics
stem: A 55-year-old man 3 days after bowel surgery has blood pressure of 80/42 mm Hg, pulse 122/min, a central venous pressure of 2 mm Hg, and urine output of 15 mL/h. Septic and hemorrhagic shock are both being considered.
oneliner: 55M + 3 days after bowel surgery + BP 80/42 + pulse 122 + CVP 2 + urine output 15 mL/h → septic or hemorrhagic shock?
ask: Which single finding favours septic over hemorrhagic shock?

options.A: A blood pressure of 80/42 mm Hg

whyNot.A: **Low blood pressure** is the definition of both
whyNot.C: **A CVP of 2** occurs in both, from vasodilation or volume loss
whyNot.D: **A urine output of 15 mL/h** reflects poor renal perfusion in both

why: Sepsis releases nitric oxide and cytokines that dilate arterioles, so **SVR is low, the skin is warm and flushed, and output is high early**. Bleeding does the reverse: vasoconstriction, cool skin and low output.

set_title: Febrile child with rash, red eyes or joints: which one hits the heart
stem: A 4-year-old boy has had fever above 39 C for 6 days. He has a red rash on the trunk, a strawberry tongue and a 2-cm cervical lymph node. Examination also shows exudative tonsillitis, and a rapid streptococcal antigen test is positive.
oneliner: 4M + fever >39 C for 6 days + trunk rash + strawberry tongue + 2-cm cervical node + exudative tonsillitis, positive rapid strep test → ?
ask: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

whyNot.B: Kawasaki disease gives **non-exudative conjunctivitis** and no tonsillar exudate; he has exudative tonsillitis and a positive strep test
whyNot.C: Rheumatic fever starts **2-4 weeks after** the sore throat with arthritis or carditis; his throat infection is active now
whyNot.D: Juvenile arthritis needs **arthritis lasting over 6 weeks**; his illness is 6 days old
whyNot.E: Erythema multiforme has **target lesions**; he has a trunk rash with exudative tonsillitis

why: One change from the Kawasaki boy: instead of conjunctivitis he has **exudative tonsillitis with a positive streptococcal test**. Group A streptococci making pyrogenic (erythrogenic) exotoxin cause the fever, strawberry tongue and a rash that feels like **sandpaper** and spares the skin around the mouth.

stem: A 29-year-old woman has had 2 weeks of fever and fatigue. She has rheumatic mitral valve disease. Her only recent procedure was a root canal 1 month ago. A new murmur is heard, the lungs are clear, and blood cultures are positive.
oneliner: 29F + 2 weeks fever + rheumatic mitral valve + root canal 1 month ago + new murmur + clear lungs → ?
ask: Which of the following is the most likely causal organism?

whyNot.A: S aureus follows **skin entry or injection drug use** and runs an acute course; her only exposure was dental work and her illness is subacute
whyNot.B: Enterococcus follows **genitourinary or bowel instrumentation**; her only procedure was dental
whyNot.D: S gallolyticus comes from the **colon** and points to colonic neoplasia in older adults; she is 29 and her procedure was dental
whyNot.E: Pneumococcus is a **rare cause that comes with pneumonia**; her lungs are clear and her source was dental

why: Dental work releases mouth streptococci into the blood, and they settle on a valve already damaged by rheumatic disease, giving a **subacute illness after a dental procedure**. In the laboratory they are alpha-hemolytic, optochin-resistant and bile-insoluble, which separates them from the pneumococcus.

set_title: Very high white count or blasts: reaction, CML or acute leukemia
stem: A 17-year-old girl has had a week of fever and sore throat with enlarged cervical lymph nodes. The leukocyte count is 18,000/mm3. Infectious mononucleosis and acute myeloid leukemia are both being considered.
oneliner: 17F + 1 week of fever and sore throat + cervical nodes + WBC 18,000 → mononucleosis or AML?
ask: Which single finding favours infectious mononucleosis over acute myeloid leukemia?

whyNot.E: **A raised white count** occurs in both

why: EBV infects B cells through CD21, and the reactive CD8+ T cells that respond appear as large atypical lymphocytes. Heterophile antibodies, which agglutinate sheep or horse red cells, appear, so **a positive heterophile (Monospot) test** points to mononucleosis; leukemia does not produce them.

set_title: Painful urination or fever with pus in the urine: urethra, bladder, prostate or kidney
stem: A 22-year-old woman has had 3 days of burning with urination and urinary frequency. Her temperature is 37.0°C and she has no flank pain. Urine microscopy shows many white cells, and a urine culture has been sent. Chlamydial urethritis and bacterial cystitis are both being considered.

options.A: Many white cells on urine microscopy
options.B: Burning pain with urination for 3 days
options.E: A temperature of 37.0°C and no flank pain

whyNot.E: Both stay **afebrile with no flank pain** when infection is confined to the lower tract

why: Chlamydia trachomatis is an obligate intracellular organism that does not grow on routine urine culture media. Pyuria with **no growth on routine culture** (sterile pyuria) points to chlamydial or gonococcal urethritis, while cystitis grows a coliform.

set_title: Weak, thin and hypotensive: which cause of adrenal insufficiency
stem: A 19-year-old man has low blood pressure, a serum sodium of 127 mEq/L, a potassium of 6.0 mEq/L and a low cortisol concentration. Waterhouse-Friderichsen syndrome and autoimmune adrenalitis are both being considered.
oneliner: 19M + hypotension + Na 127 + K 6.0 + low cortisol → WFS or autoimmune adrenalitis?
ask: Which single finding favors Waterhouse-Friderichsen syndrome over autoimmune adrenalitis?

whyNot.A: Pigmentation needs weeks of **high ACTH** and favors **autoimmune adrenalitis**
whyNot.B: A slow course with weight loss favors **autoimmune adrenalitis**
whyNot.C: Both disorders destroy the cortex, and the stem already gives a **low cortisol**
whyNot.D: Both disorders lose aldosterone, and the stem already gives a **potassium of 6.0**

why: Meningococcemia triggers DIC and bilateral adrenal hemorrhage, so cortisol and aldosterone fall in hours. **Fever with spreading purpura and shock** points to Waterhouse-Friderichsen syndrome; autoimmune adrenalitis builds over months.

set_title: Runny nose, sore throat or fever with cough: which virus, or not an infection at all
stem: A 6-year-old girl has had fever of 38.9 C, sore throat and red, watery eyes for 3 days. Several children at her summer swim camp have the same illness.
oneliner: 6F + fever 38.9 C + sore throat + red watery eyes for 3 days + sick children at swim camp → ?
ask: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

whyNot.B: Influenza gives abrupt fever with severe muscle aches and a dry cough and not red eyes; she has **sore throat with red, watery eyes**
whyNot.C: Allergic rhinitis causes itchy watery eyes without fever; she has a **fever of 38.9 C** and a camp outbreak
whyNot.D: A cold causes little fever and spares the eyes; she has **fever of 38.9 C with red eyes**
whyNot.E: Rhinitis medicamentosa follows topical decongestant use and causes no fever; she has **fever, sore throat and red eyes** in an outbreak

why: **Fever with pharyngitis and conjunctivitis**, spread among children at a swim camp, is pharyngoconjunctival fever. Adenovirus is a non-enveloped double-stranded DNA virus; it also causes acute hemorrhagic cystitis and epidemic keratoconjunctivitis.

set_title: Stridor, wheeze or hoarseness in a child (or a hoarse smoker): which airway disease
stem: A 3-year-old girl has fever and noisy breathing. She has inspiratory stridor. A lateral neck x-ray shows a swollen epiglottis.
oneliner: 3F + fever + inspiratory stridor + swollen epiglottis on lateral neck x-ray → ?
ask: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

whyNot.B: Bronchiolitis is small-airway disease with wheezing and crackles; she has **inspiratory stridor** and a swollen epiglottis
whyNot.C: Croup narrows the airway below the cords (steeple sign on a frontal film); the lateral film here shows a **swollen epiglottis**
whyNot.D: Papillomatosis gives weeks of hoarseness without fever; she has **fever** and a swollen epiglottis
whyNot.E: Laryngeal carcinoma is a disease of older smokers; this patient is **3 years old with fever**

why: Same child, one change: the lateral film now shows a swollen epiglottis (**thumb sign**). Epiglottitis is caused by Haemophilus influenzae type b, which has a polysaccharide capsule, and mainly affects unvaccinated children. Secure the airway before anything else.

set_title: Pneumonia after a transplant or with AIDS: which opportunist, or the graft
stem: A 36-year-old woman has had fever for 6 days and has coughed up blood-streaked sputum. She is on day 18 of chemotherapy for acute myeloid leukemia, and her neutrophil count is 200/uL. A chest CT shows several nodules, each surrounded by a halo of ground glass. A biopsy shows septate hyphae branching at acute angles within vessel walls.
oneliner: 36F + fever and blood-streaked sputum + chemotherapy for leukemia with neutrophils 200/uL + halo nodules on CT + septate hyphae branching at acute angles in vessels → ?
ask: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

whyNot.A: Cytomegalovirus shows owl-eye inclusions with interstitial infiltrates; her biopsy shows **septate hyphae**
whyNot.B: Pneumocystis shows cysts in a foamy exudate with diffuse opacities; she has **halo nodules with hyphae**
whyNot.C: A post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder needs a transplant; she is on **chemotherapy for leukemia**
whyNot.E: Rejection needs a graft; she is on **chemotherapy for leukemia** and her biopsy shows hyphae

why: Profound **neutropenia**, halo nodules and **septate hyphae branching at acute angles** invading vessels is invasive aspergillosis. Hemoptysis comes from angioinvasion and infarction, and voriconazole is the treatment.
